newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin names liberal ally Chubais first deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin names liberal ally Chubais first deputy PM.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin appointed his liberal aide and ally Anatoly Chubais to the post of first deputy prime minister, the Kremlin said on Friday.
"The president of the Russian Federation Boris Nikolayevich Yeltsin has issued an order appointing Anatoly Borisovich Chubais first deputy prime minister," a Kremlin spokesman said by telephone.
Another Yeltsin decree relieved Chubais of his current job as head of the Kremlin administration, the spokesman said. There was no announcement of an immediate replacement.
The appointment of Chubais to the post of first deputy prime mimister in charge of economic reforms has been widely expected.

On Thursday Yeltsin marked his return to the helm of power after eight months of illness with a determined and strong state of the nation speech to parliament in which he promised to reshuffle and streamline the government, bring order and root out top-level corruption.
Chubais, 41, is respected in the West as a dedicated reformer. He is also an excellent administrator and organiser.
But the communist-dominated opposition loathe him for his role in Yeltsin's re-election campaign last year and also accuse him of selling off Russia's state-owned firms cheaply during privatisation.
